description: An interstellar society with competing planetary governments, advanced biotechnology, megacorporations, alien species and complex economic systems. I begin as an indebted freighter mechanic on an orbital station.

core.name: The Solvay Concord
core.tagline: Where gravity bends, contracts shift, and trust is currency
core.premise: A fractured interstellar federation of planetary governments, megacorporations, and alien species, bound by shared economic systems and political rivalries, where biological engineering shapes society and trade is governed by biological credit, not money.
core.tone: Calmly dystopian, precise, grounded in bureaucratic realism,
core.intro: You wake to the hum of coolant pipes and the smell of ozone—your fingers still calloused from welding the cargo bay’s failing reactor seal. The station’s central monitor flickers: 'Debt Balance: 7.3 biocredits. Next payment due in 3.4 hours. Status: Delinquent.' You’re on the lower deck of the orbital logistics hub Solvay-9, a rusted ring of steel and bio-mesh suspended in the void between Mars and Titan, where freighters like yours move like insects in a vast, silent economy

special_rules.name: Gravity Tuning
special_rules.summary: You can tune gravity in a cargo module by inserting a gravity-tuning seed and running it through a tissue-sense sensor. This temporarily stabilizes a

on_success.text: The seed reacts to the local gravity field — a small batch of stabilizer fiber is formed.
The fiber is weak and must be used immediately or degrade.

on_failure.text: You feel a sudden lurch — your hands tremble, and a vial of healing fluid leaks from your glove.

special_rules.name: Biocredit Resonance
special_rules.summary: When you use a trust calibration cube near a biocredit exchange, you can briefly detect if someone is lying about their balance. It requires a live bi

on_success.text: The cube emits a soft hum — a nearby trader is over-declaring their biocredit balance by 40%.
You gain 10% trust with Darien Vey, who now believes you’re honest.

on_failure.text: The cube flickers and shorts out — you’re left with a small puddle of gel on your workbench.

special_rules.name: Self-Healing Adaptation
special_rules.summary: If you're injured, you can use a healing-by-adaptation vial to trigger a biological healing cascade in your tissues. This works best after minor burns

on_success.text: Your arm regenerates tissue — you feel lighter, stronger.
The vial was drawn from your own tissue — it now cannot be used again.

on_failure.text: The vial explodes in your hand — the probe is damaged and cannot be used for diagnostics.
